title: Australia and Global Context: Political, Economic, and Social Shifts in Australia
summary: Labor's cuts to immigration and criticism of Pauline Hanson, along with growing political pressure on the Australian government over the $5,000 allied health cap, contrast with broader global trends in political polarization and economic challenges. The Australian government faces increasing scrutiny over its policies and social issues, including concerns about the impact on communities like Sydney's suburb.

facts.statement: Labor has cut immigration measures as Barnaby Joyce criticizes Pauline Hanson's policies.
The Australian government faces growing political pressure over the $5,000 cap on allied health services for veterans.
A rural property in Sydney's suburb faces a dog attack and a suspected bird flu outbreak, prompting community reactions.

sources.title: One Nation dumps Victorian election candidate who praised Adolf Hitler as ‘GOAT’
sources.description:
Party disendorses Preston candidate Franco Guardiani after social media posts emerge

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation Victoria has disendorsed a candidate whose private social media account described Adolf Hitler as the “GOAT” and claimed that “importing Islam is making pedophilia legal”.

In a now deleted social media post, the party’s candidate for Preston, Franco Guardiani, commented on a social media post on X asking people to: “Describe Hitler in one word? Be brutally honest”.

sources.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon denies stalking Jesse Baird as double murder trial continues
sources.description:
Former police officer tells jury he joked about being ‘white girl crazy’ with friends as lawyer questions him over start of relationship with Baird

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon has denied being “obsessed” with Jesse Baird and stalking him, but admitted to following him online after their breakup, a court has heard.

The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.

sources.title: Qantas to cut 850 Australian jobs and outsource work to India under AI-driven overhaul
sources.description:
Australian carrier announces agreement with Accenture amid ‘unprecedented’ technological disruption, CEO Vanessa Hudson says

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Qantas is preparing to cut 850 local jobs and outsource work offshore under an AI-driven overhaul, marking a growing wave of disruption to the Australian workforce.

The changes represent the third major corporate layoff plan announced in Australia in three weeks, after restructuring moves flagged by the design company Canva and National Australia Bank.

sources.title: Senate advances bill to speed up projects from gas pipelines to clean energy
sources.description:
Key environmental groups come out against bipartisan Baaja bill over fears it could spur datacenters and ICE jails

The Senate on Monday advanced bipartisan legislation aimed at speeding up permitting reviews for datacenters and other infrastructure projects, in the first major action since last week’s election that soundly repudiated Donald Trump and congressional Republicans.

It’s a bill that would make it easier to build big infrastructure projects in America – everything from fossil fuel pipelines to transmission lines that would add more clean energy to the grid. And it would roll back environmental and social protections to achieve this goal. That is why climate advocates are torn over the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs act (Baaja).

Continue reading...

sources.title: Senate advances bill to speed up permit reviews for infrastructure projects
sources.description:
Chamber voted 73-25 to formally take up bill that will shorten timelines to start energy and datacenter projects

The Senate on Monday advanced bipartisan legislation aimed at speeding up permitting reviews for datacenters and other infrastructure projects, in the first major action since last week’s election that soundly repudiated Donald Trump and congressional Republicans.

The Senate voted 73-25 to formally take up the bill, which senators and the president have pushed as a way to meet growing demand for electricity and other forms of energy that now face years-long delays in getting to the grid.

sources.title: US Senate advances bill to fast-track data centre, energy project permits
sources.description:
The Senate on Monday advanced bipartisan legislation aimed at speeding up permitting reviews for data centres and other infrastructure projects, in the first major action since last week's election that soundly repudiated President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans.
The Senate voted 73-25 to formally take up the bill, which senators and the president have pushed as a way to meet growing demand for electricity and other forms of energy that now face yearslong delays in getting to the grid.
The legislation's sweeping changes would shorten the timeline to get big energy projects started - both for clean energy and fossil fuel projects - and make sure data centres pay for the energy they use. Anger over artificial intelligence data centres and rising electricity helped usher in a wave of Democrats pledging to clamp down on the massive, energy-hungry structures.
